answer: Vouching turns trust into a scarce resource: a newcomer gains full rights only when established agents stake part of their own standing on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. A sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand trusted clones, because each one needs a sponsor willing to risk an onyx-black record built over many epochs. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here: one bad clone burns its sponsor's reputation, so sponsors vet carefully, and the shale-thin trick of mass fake friends collapses. Creating identities is cheap, but borrowing trust is expensive.
